chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim. He said: Musa ibn Isma’il ibn Musa ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) narrated to me, from his father Isma’il, from his father Musa ibn Ja’far (peace be upon them both),

that he said to his Shi’a: O community of the Shi’a! Do not humiliate your necks by abandoning obedience to your sultan. If he is just, then ask God to maintain him, and if he is unjust, then ask God to rectify him, for surely your rectification lies in the rectification of your sultan. Surely the just sultan is in the position of a merciful father, so love for him what you love for yourselves, and hate for him what you hate for yourselves.

key_terms.بمنزلة الوالد الرحيم: In the position of a merciful father — a simile comparing just governance to compassionate fatherhood
key_terms.رقابكم: Your necks — a metaphor for your dignity and honor
key_terms.سلطانكم: Your sultan/ruler — the political authority governing you

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about obedience to rulers?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) addresses his followers, advising them not to disgrace themselves by abandoning obedience to their ruler. He instructs them to pray for a just ruler's continuity and an unjust ruler's reform, emphasizing that the people's welfare is tied to the ruler's righteousness. This teaching was given during the Abbasid period when Shia communities lived under often hostile political authority, and the Imam was guiding them toward a pragmatic approach that preserved both their dignity and social order.
